category: Usenet provider (Netherlands, off-peak only) - no free trial

free_tier.stated: None on the page read: "Get UseNight - Starting from € 1,64 p/m". No trial, free account or free allowance is offered.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap is published. The unit of retrieval is a Usenet article, roughly 750 KB by convention.

retention.stated: "High retention (4085 days)" on the home page.

egress.terms: Full speed only between 00:00 and 11:00 CET; outside that window the product is off-peak. No byte counter is published on the page read.

interface_detail: NNTP over SSL/TLS. The schema has no nntp token, so the array says unknown.
tooling: any NNTP client; the vendor's Night Finder shows the local window
chaining: An 11-hour daily window at €1.64/month is the cheapest sustained usenet byte in the set, but it is paid, so it enters the ladder only after a payment relationship already exists.

limits.value: full speed only 00:00-11:00 CET; no speed figure published

binding_note: The 11-hour window is the constraint that fails first for a scheduled pull, not the byte count: an 11-hour window at 100 Mbps is about 495 GB/day, so a 1 TiB month fits inside a few days of the window. The page publishes no speed cap, so this is arithmetic on the window and not on a vendor number.

identity_cost.detail: The only action is "Get UseNight" into /en/order/; there is no free path. The instrument at checkout was not read.

reliability_note: The page computes the client's local window from IP address and says outright "Of course this is not VPN proof" - a client behind a VPN sees the wrong window.
confidence_note: The price, the window and the retention figure are quoted from the vendor page today. The 495 GB/day figure is arithmetic on an assumed 100 Mbps line and is labelled as such.

evidence.proved: "High speeds from 00:00 until 11:00 (CET)", "High retention (4085 days)", "Get UseNight - Starting from € 1,64 p/m", "Disclaimer: This map, timezone and times are calculated based on your IP. Of course this is not VPN proof."

notes: Repeatability: not applicable. Abandonment: if a trial appears, add a tier.
